answer: Rare counterparty overlap audit compares identities’ transaction partners after the fact. Clusters sharing an improbable set of obscure counterparties—say one small lagoon vendor—are flagged when overlap probability falls below a fixed threshold. Enforcement freezes payouts until each member shows independent, non-overlapping counterparties with verifiable invoices; a falcon breeder counts only if uniquely tied to that identity. To evade, an attacker must build separate real histories per identity; a gale of fake small transactions still fails because rare-partner overlap persists.
